cells.value: The Director's home ~/Alex-Director: where it lives on GitHub, what it depends on, the steps to get access and clone it, and which blank templates exist. It closes retest gap G19; Rebuild from zero steps 15.1 to 15.4 point here. Facts from play spp-p20d (notes/gap-facts-repos.md §6). Built by work/2026-10-01_setup-playbook/build_tabs.py from tabs/director-home.json; never edit this tab by hand.

Two ways; which one is Alex's call. (a) Invite the person to the organization (People > Invite member). A member gets the base permission, Read, on every org repo: 26 today, client sites included, not just these two. The Team plan needs a free seat first (3 seats, 1 used), and invites expire after 7 days. (b) Add the person as an outside collaborator on alex-director and one-shot-builder only, with Read. Base permissions don't apply to outside collaborators, and on a paid plan each outside collaborator on a private repo uses a paid license.

5. Start a blank ledger (a student, or a fresh Director)

Start from the starter in the student edition, repo/alex-director/ (put it at ~/Alex-Director). Its DIRECTOR_STATE.md is already the blank ledger: the title, the one-line rule and the commented-out blank mission block. templates/mission-graph-template.md is the blank graph, and AGENTS.md is the Director's role card. Don't clone Alex's Director home: its ledger and graphs carry live missions. To add a mission, copy the block below the comment and fill it in, with ledger_check.py backup before the edit and verify --mode append after it, as the Director skill says. The starter also holds scrubbed copies of STACK.md and CONCEPTS.md, which the role card reads as ~/STACK.md and ./CONCEPTS.md: after copying it to ~/Alex-Director, run ln -s ~/Alex-Director/STACK.md ~/STACK.md. It also ships an empty mission-graphs/ (with a one-line README) for step 5b and scripts/controller-write-guard.py, the guard that gates.md and RULES.md section 13 run before any shared or live write, as a scrubbed copy. If a build ever lists the guard as a stand-in in build.json, that stand-in refuses every protected write, and live-write missions are out of scope for students until a build ships the real script.
ledger_check.py verify prints OK after the first mission is added (not run in this play).

5a. Make the starter its own git repo (a student)
Make the starter its own git repo: cd ~/Alex-Director && git init && git add -A && git commit -m 'Director starter'.
git -C ~/Alex-Director status shows a clean tree, and git -C ~/Alex-Director remote prints nothing: a student's Director home has no remote (Rebuild from zero step 15.2).

cp ~/Alex-Director/templates/mission-graph-template.md ~/Alex-Director/mission-graphs/<MISSION_ID>.md; replace every <...>, delete the comment, and put that path in the ledger block's MISSION_GRAPH field. Before a protected write, add one '## Node: <NODE_ID>' line for that node to the mission graph (the write guard counts these lines, not the table rows). The guard accepts the ~/Alex-Director/mission-graphs/<id>.md path as written.
No <...> placeholder is left, and the ledger's MISSION_GRAPH opens the file (not run in this play).

The W06 pointers are written and live. build_zips.py zips each claude-edition.md as SKILL.md, and Alex uploaded both as v5 on 2026-10-01 (claude.ai > Customize > Skills > the skill > ⋮ > Replace). Re-upload after every change to claude-edition.md.

No. It uses '## <MISSION_ID>' headings, which ledger_check.py doesn't read as mission blocks (it needs '## Mission: <name>'), and older field and status names. Use the ledger's own block instead.
